Just wanted to offer some tips on your smoker if you get a new one.

  1. Always clean out the firebox after a cook. I clear mine out the morning after when it's cooled down.
  2. Keep it out of rain or use a rain cover.

I saw a video from a guy that builds custom smokers professionally and said the fire box is the first thing to go because people leave the ashes in the firebox. If rain gets into it (or even just the general humidity in the summer) the moisture will mix with the ashes and create a caustic mix that eats into the metal. The guy is right because I've been cleaning mine religiously and not a spot of rust until one time I didn't get a chance to clean it out (thunderstorms rolled in the morning after) and sure enough; the rain got in and several spots of rust formed. I had to brush it clean and re-oil it.

If you decide to go with a new one, get the heaviest (lowest gauge steel) model you can. Not one of those cheap ass Oklahoma Joe's smokers that are now made in China. OK Joe's used to be one of the best smokers on the market until he sold it off to Char-Broil, which of course, outsourced the manufacturing to the Chinese. Now, they're shit and the thin ass steel they are made from won't hold heat for nothing. You'll be chunking in wood constantly just trying to maintain temperature.

Good luck with your projects fellow Goat!
